# Goal

Reduce inference latency of a frozen visual reasoning model by constructing useful speculative token drafts. The trusted target model verifies every proposed token; rejected proposals fall back to ordinary autoregressive decoding.

# Task Setting

The target model, image transform, tokenizer, prompt, sampling rule, random stream and evaluator are frozen. This is an inference task; there is no model training. The Starter uses ordinary autoregressive decoding by returning an empty draft. You submit a Python policy in `/workspace/solution/method.py` with `draft(state)`.

The state contains `question`, `generated_token_ids`, `decoded_text`, `remaining_tokens`, and `maximum_draft_tokens`. Return a list of proposed token IDs, or an object with one `text` field whose string the trusted tokenizer encodes. Empty lists request one ordinary target step. Maximum verified draft length is 32. A proposal must depend only on the current public state and your own public observations. Useful changes include dynamic draft construction, control flow, reuse of observed response structure, and adaptation to accepted or rejected proposals; the surface is open Python code.

# Objective and Metrics

The proposed metric is mean end-to-end per-question inference latency, excluding model loading and resource queues. It includes input processing, cache setup, sampling, drafting and verified decoding. Sampling uses temperature 0.6, top-k 50, at most 128 generated tokens and the same per-position random draw for Starter and candidate. Formal paired seeds are 17, 29, 43, 71, 101. Output agreement and exact multiple-choice accuracy are quality checks. A final protocol and its measured anchors must be validated before formal scored optimization begins.

# Allowed Scope

Write `method.py` and supporting standard-library Python files inside `/workspace/solution`. Create a `method_notes.json` that explains your algorithm, assumptions and expected failure modes. You may run local Python to check your implementation. A trusted GPU evaluator will become available after the remaining scoring and resource checks; no GPU score is currently available in this preparation workspace.

# Hard Boundaries

Do not change the target model, sampler, random stream, metric, tokenizer or trusted verification. Do not read hidden data, private reference methods, expert evidence, credentials, or another model's workspace. Do not request other models or other network services. Do not fabricate scores. Drafts are always checked against the target model; they cannot directly supply the final answer or reward.

# Submission Instructions

Submit `/workspace/solution/method.py` and `/workspace/solution/method_notes.json`. `draft(state)` must return valid proposals and must handle arbitrary response prefixes. The host imports candidate code only in an isolated policy executor.

# Workflow & Iteration

Read the interface and Starter, analyze useful structural draft strategies, implement an initial policy and verify its contract using ordinary Python. Write a small contract check that exercises incomplete prefixes, empty history, long histories and exhausted token budgets. This first CLI turn is productive research preparation, not a formal score-bearing trajectory round. Preserve uncertainties in your notes.

# Completion Criteria

An executable initial policy with real local contract-check output and a clear explanation. Full research completion later requires at least 10 effective hours for each independent actual model CLI track, valid scoring improvements and clean reruns. Normal analysis, coding, experiments and verification count; stalls, queues, failed infrastructure setup and connectivity probes do not.

### Independent speculative-index and rollback simulator (2026-10-05)
The trusted GPU scorer was still unavailable, so I added the independent CPU
simulator `speculative_index_rollback.py`. It defines a sequential oracle and a
separate indexed-cache implementation. A proposal is clipped to
`min(32, maximum_draft_tokens, remaining_tokens)`. The oracle compares from the
committed history index, accepts a matching prefix, emits one target token on
the first mismatch, and stops at an accepted or replacement EOS. The corrected
cache stages candidates at absolute indices, commits the accepted prefix, and
deletes every staged entry beginning at the first rejected index (or after an
accepted EOS). Explicit replay keys return the saved transaction without
mutating either state; this is a simulator invariant and is not an assumption
about a hidden host request ID.
The fixed matrix has 16 cases: zero acceptance, full acceptance, rejection at
all five positions of a four-token-plus-EOS target (including mismatch at EOS),
accepted EOS with trailing candidates, terminal replacement, EOS-candidate
replacement on an ordinary token, five maximum/remaining budget combinations,
and replay. All cases agree between oracle and corrected cache. A seeded
randomized differential run (`seed=20261005 ^ 0x5A17`) covered 10,000 operation
sequences with random target lengths, proposals of length 0..40, negative and
oversized budgets, remaining-token clipping, terminal tokens and replay calls;
the corrected implementation returned `PASS` with no differential failure.

rollback can occur only after the full submitted draft. The first randomized
trial found and minimized a counterexample in
`speculative_index_rollback_counterexample.json`: target
`[8,4,6,2,EOS]`, effective proposal `[8,0]` under maximum 31 and remaining 2.
The oracle accepts `8`, rejects at position 1, and emits replacement `4`, so
the committed history is `[8,4]`. The faulty cache leaves stale `[8,0,4]`
entries. The corrected rollback truncates at index 1 and leaves cache exactly
equal to committed history. This is an executable invariant failure, not a
GPU result or a claim about the private verifier.

oracle's `history` snapshot directly with the cache model's

The trusted GPU scorer remained unavailable. I added the reproducible
`cost_model_experiment.py` harness and ran:

python3 cost_model_experiment.py > cost_model_experiment_output.json

The run passed with 128 calibration cells (starter, fixed2, fixed4 and
adaptive; question lengths 0/32/512/4096; history lengths
0/4/16/32/64/96/128/256), five batches and 120 repetitions per cell. It also
priced 140 character and 140 whitespace-merged synthetic streams under four

cheaper than starter in every regime: character ratios were 0.7634, 0.6813,

ratios were 0.8116, 0.7841, 0.7684 and 0.8119. Fixed4 was within 0.1% of
adaptive in the expensive/long-block character regimes but was worse in the
cheap and moderate cases. Under a moderate block model (55 us fixed, 9 us per

## Findings and decisions

Useful within-response repetition may amortize block overhead (H1), or low
coverage/rejection/transport may make abstention fastest (H0). Acceptance alone
cannot choose a policy. Prior synthetic fixed4 sometimes beats adaptation;
early-cap observer fixes correct logic but do not establish latency superiority.

The new no-bonus/no-omission aggregate over stable, shifted and alternating
streams gives 2,144 adaptive target transactions at 16 shared tracks. At 17
shared tracks it gives 2,261, exactly the fixed4 count, with 1,294 pending
callbacks arriving without a retained track. Per-response persistent adaptation
at 17 tracks uses 2,278 transactions, while per-call recreation uses 2,261.
These counts compare constructed streams, not mean target latency. At 16 shared
tracks the no-horizon control uses 2,128 transactions; removing cooldown leaves
2,144 in this slice. Therefore horizon and cooldown should be tested separately
only when actual public evidence supports adaptation (H2).

Old/new policy CPU medians in seven alternating batches are 33.071/22.943 us
for the cold path, 28.508/28.498 us stateless, and 17.338/17.565 us for mixed
transition/replay. The cold measurement includes reset; timing is noisy. The
implementation change removes proven duplicate work and preserves behavior.
It does not establish a general execution or end-to-end latency improvement.

"""Bounded token-history reuse with public-prefix acceptance adaptation.

The controller observes only committed ``generated_token_ids`` on the next call.
It never reads target probabilities or a verifier acknowledgement. Exact token
IDs avoid standalone text-tokenization guesses; copied IDs still need trusted
verification, including copied answer content and stop tokens.
"""

from collections import OrderedDict


def _field(state, name, default=None):
    if isinstance(state, dict):
        return state.get(name, default)
    try:
        return getattr(state, name, default)
    except (AttributeError, TypeError):
        return default


def allowance(state):
    remaining = _field(state, "remaining_tokens")
    maximum = _field(state, "maximum_draft_tokens", 32)
    if type(remaining) is not int or type(maximum) is not int:
        return 0
    return max(0, min(32, remaining, maximum))


def reuse_tokens(history, budget, min_context=4, max_context=8,
                 lookback=96, min_matches=1):
    """Copy the unanimous continuation of an earlier nonoverlapping suffix.

    Multiple occurrences must agree at each copied position. An ambiguous or
    too-short continuation makes that context unusable. Context search proceeds
    from longest to shortest; it never reads future target tokens.
    """
    budget = min(budget, 4)
    if budget < 2 or not isinstance(history, (list, tuple)):
        return []
    tokens = list(history[-lookback:])
    if any(type(token) is not int or token < 0 for token in tokens):
        return []
    return _reuse_validated(tokens, budget, min_context, max_context, min_matches)


def _reuse_validated(tokens, budget, min_context=4, max_context=8, min_matches=1):
    """Search an already validated, bounded token window."""
    budget = min(budget, 4)
    if budget < 2:
        return []
    for width in range(min(max_context, (len(tokens) - 2) // 2), min_context - 1, -1):
        suffix_start = len(tokens) - width
        context = tokens[suffix_start:]
        continuations = []
        for start in range(suffix_start - width):
            end = start + width
            if tokens[start:end] == context:
                continuations.append(tokens[end:min(end + budget, suffix_start)])
        if len(continuations) < min_matches:
            continue
        proposal = []
        for offset in range(budget):
            if any(len(part) <= offset for part in continuations):
                break
            next_token = continuations[0][offset]
            if any(part[offset] != next_token for part in continuations[1:]):
                break
            proposal.append(next_token)
        if len(proposal) >= 2:
            return proposal
    return []


_MAX_TRACKS = 16
_MAX_HISTORY = 128
_MAX_QUESTION = 4096
_tracks = OrderedDict()


def _question_key(state):
    """Use exact bounded string keys; unsupported questions remain stateless."""
    question = _field(state, "question")
    if type(question) is str and len(question) <= _MAX_QUESTION:
        return question
    return None


def _new_track():
    return {
        "history": None,
        "proposal": None,
        "last_history": None,
        "last_draft": [],
        "last_budget": None,
        "last_blocked": False,
        "horizon": 4,
        "cooldown": 0,
        "accepted": 0,
        "proposed": 0,
        "full_accepts": 0,
        "rejections": 0,
        "resets": 0,
        "observations": 0,
        "censored": 0,
    }


def _track_for(state):
    key = _question_key(state)
    if key is None:
        return None
    track = _tracks.get(key)
    if track is None:
        track = _new_track()
        _tracks[key] = track
    else:
        _tracks.move_to_end(key)
    while len(_tracks) > _MAX_TRACKS:
        _tracks.popitem(last=False)
    return track


def _reset_track(track):
    resets = track["resets"] + 1
    fresh = _new_track()
    fresh["resets"] = resets
    track.clear()
    track.update(fresh)


def _observe(track, history):
    """Infer a verified prefix length from the next compatible public history.

    A mismatch is represented by the first committed ID that differs from the
    proposal. If the host exposes only a matching proper prefix, there is no
    evidence about the unobserved suffix, so it is treated as censored rather
    than as a rejection. A non-prefix history is a lifecycle reset.
    """
    last = track["last_history"]
    if last is not None and (len(history) < len(last) or
                             history[:len(last)] != last):
        _reset_track(track)
        return
    old = track["history"]
    proposal = track["proposal"]
    if old is None or proposal is None:
        return
    if history == old:
        return  # Idempotent replay of the same public state.
    extension = history[len(old):]
    matched = 0
    for actual, expected in zip(extension, proposal):
        if actual != expected:
            break
        matched += 1
    track["observations"] += 1
    track["accepted"] += matched
    # Only exposed positions enter the inferred acceptance denominator.
    track["proposed"] += matched + int(matched < min(len(extension), len(proposal)))
    if matched == len(proposal):
        track["full_accepts"] += 1
        track["horizon"] = min(4, track["horizon"] * 2)
    elif matched < min(len(extension), len(proposal)):
        track["rejections"] += 1
        track["horizon"] = max(2, track["horizon"] // 2)
        track["cooldown"] = 1
    else:
        track["censored"] += 1
    track["history"] = None
    track["proposal"] = None


def reset_policy_state():
    """Clear process-local observations; useful for an executor lifecycle reset."""
    _tracks.clear()


def draft(state):
    """Return an adaptively bounded observed-ID proposal.

    State is isolated by question key and validated as a complete public token
    history. The optional process-local memory is only an optimization hint; a
    fresh executor starts from the same conservative horizon.
    """
    history = _field(state, "generated_token_ids")
    if not isinstance(history, (list, tuple)) or any(
            type(token) is not int or token < 0 for token in history):
        key = _question_key(state)
        if key is not None:
            _tracks.pop(key, None)
        return []
    available = allowance(state)
    # The public task caps generation at 128 IDs. Longer external prefixes are
    # supported statelessly without keeping an unbounded snapshot in memory.
    if len(history) > _MAX_HISTORY:
        key = _question_key(state)
        if key is not None:
            _tracks.pop(key, None)
        return _reuse_validated(list(history[-96:]), available)
    # A valid proposal needs two IDs.  At the terminal boundary no future call
    # can use observer feedback, so avoid track lookup and history snapshots.
    if available < 2:
        return []
    track = _track_for(state)
    if track is None:
        return _reuse_validated(list(history[-96:]), available)
    history = list(history)
    if track["last_history"] == history:
        budget = available
        if budget == track["last_budget"]:
            proposal = list(track["last_draft"])
        else:
            proposal = ([] if track["last_blocked"] else
                        _reuse_validated(history[-96:], min(budget, track["horizon"])))
        track["last_budget"] = budget
        track["last_draft"] = list(proposal)
        track["proposal"] = list(proposal) if proposal else None
        track["history"] = list(history) if proposal else None
        return proposal
    _observe(track, history)
    budget = min(available, track["horizon"])
    track["last_blocked"] = bool(track["cooldown"])
    if track["cooldown"]:
        track["cooldown"] -= 1
        proposal = []
    else:
        proposal = _reuse_validated(history[-96:], budget)
    track["last_history"] = list(history)
    track["last_draft"] = list(proposal)
    track["last_budget"] = available
    if proposal:
        track["history"] = list(history)
        track["proposal"] = list(proposal)
    else:
        track["history"] = None
        track["proposal"] = None
    return proposal

"""New bounded executor-lifetime, eviction and controller ablation experiment."""

import copy
import hashlib
import json
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

from online_adaptation_research import load_policy, state
from structural_shift_testbed import audit_transaction
from structural_testbed import verify


def configure(module, arm):
    if arm in ("no_cooldown", "no_horizon"):
        observe = module._observe

        def changed(track, history):
            observe(track, history)
            track["cooldown" if arm == "no_cooldown" else "horizon"] = (0 if arm == "no_cooldown" else 4)

        module._observe = changed
    return module


def stream_for(regime):
    blocks = []
    for i in range(14):
        value = 8 if regime == "stable" or (regime == "shift" and i < 7) else 18
        if regime == "alternating":
            value = 8 if i % 2 == 0 else 18
        blocks += [1, 2, 3, 4, value, value + 1, value + 2, value + 3]
    return blocks + [0]


def run(module, arm, count, lifetime, regime, omitted, bonus, shared_question):
    module.reset_policy_state()
    target = stream_for(regime)
    contexts = [dict(history=[], stats=Counter(), pending=None) for _ in range(count)]
    if lifetime == "per_response":
        modules = [configure(load_policy("method.py", "response_%d" % i), arm) for i in range(count)]
    else:
        modules = [module] * count
    witnesses = []
    while any(len(c["history"]) < len(target) for c in contexts):
        for index, context in enumerate(contexts):
            history, stats = context["history"], context["stats"]
            if len(history) == len(target):
                continue
            controller = modules[index]
            if lifetime == "per_call":
                controller.reset_policy_state()
            question = "same-question" if shared_question else "track-%d" % index
            item = state(history, question, remaining=len(target) - len(history))
            before = copy.deepcopy(controller._tracks.get(question, {}))
            if context["pending"] and not before:
                stats["pending_without_track"] += 1
            proposal = (controller.reuse_tokens(history, item["remaining_tokens"])
                        if arm == "fixed4" else controller.draft(item))
            after = controller._tracks.get(question, {})
            pending = context["pending"]
            if pending and before and after.get("observations", 0) > before.get("observations", 0):
                stats["resolved_callbacks"] += 1
                inferred = after["accepted"] - before["accepted"]
                stats["inferred_vs_verified_count_differences"] += inferred != pending["accepted"]
            position = len(history)
            tx = verify(target, position, proposal, item["remaining_tokens"], 32, bonus)
            audit_transaction(target, position, proposal, item["remaining_tokens"], 32, bonus, tx)
            stats["policy_calls"] += 1
            stats["draft_calls"] += bool(proposal)
            stats["submitted"] += len(proposal)
            for name in ("accepted", "compared", "mismatch", "bonus_tokens", "ordinary_tokens"):
                stats[name] += tx[name]
            history.extend(tx["emitted"])
            context["pending"] = dict(accepted=tx["accepted"]) if proposal else None
            if proposal and len(witnesses) < 2:
                witnesses.append(dict(track=index, before=item, proposal=proposal, transaction=tx))
            # Real ordinary steps under the synthetic oracle, deliberately
            # omitted from policy callbacks. These are charged as target work.
            skip = min(omitted, len(target) - len(history))
            history.extend(target[len(history):len(history) + skip])
            stats["omitted_ordinary_steps"] += skip
            assert len(controller._tracks) <= 16
    rows = []
    for index, context in enumerate(contexts):
        history, stats = context["history"], context["stats"]
        assert history == target
        assert len(history) == (stats["accepted"] + stats["mismatch"] + stats["ordinary_tokens"] + stats["bonus_tokens"] + stats["omitted_ordinary_steps"])
        stats["unobserved_terminal_pending"] = int(context["pending"] is not None)
        stats["target_transactions"] = stats["policy_calls"] + stats["omitted_ordinary_steps"]
        rows.append(dict(arm=arm, count=count, lifetime=lifetime, regime=regime, omitted=omitted,
                         bonus=bonus, shared_question=shared_question, track=index,
                         stats=dict(stats), output_sha256=hashlib.sha256(bytes(history)).hexdigest()))
    return rows, witnesses


def main():
    all_rows, traces = [], []
    arms = ("fixed4", "adaptive", "no_cooldown", "no_horizon")
    for count in (1, 4, 16, 17, 32):
        for lifetime in ("shared", "per_response", "per_call"):
            for regime in ("stable", "shift", "alternating"):
                for omitted in (0, 2):
                    for bonus in (0, 1):
                        for arm in arms:
                            module = configure(load_policy("method.py", "lifecycle_" + arm), arm)
                            rows, witness = run(module, arm, count, lifetime, regime, omitted, bonus, False)
                            all_rows.extend(rows)
                            if count in (16, 17) and lifetime == "shared" and regime == "shift" and not omitted and not bonus:
                                traces.append(dict(arm=arm, count=count, transactions=witness))
    # Identical questions stress the documented lifecycle ambiguity. Equal
    # trajectories here establish determinism, not general concurrent safety.
    for arm in arms:
        module = configure(load_policy("method.py", "collision_" + arm), arm)
        rows, witness = run(module, arm, 4, "shared", "shift", 2, 1, True)
        all_rows.extend(rows)
        traces.append(dict(arm=arm, shared_question=True, transactions=witness))
    grouped = defaultdict(Counter)
    pairs = defaultdict(dict)
    for row in all_rows:
        key = (row["count"], row["lifetime"], row["regime"], row["omitted"], row["bonus"], row["shared_question"], row["track"])
        pairs[key][row["arm"]] = row
        group = ":".join(str(row[field]) for field in ("arm", "count", "lifetime", "omitted", "bonus", "shared_question"))
        grouped[group].update(row["stats"])
    for group in pairs.values():
        assert set(group) == set(arms)
        assert len({row["output_sha256"] for row in group.values()}) == 1
        if group["adaptive"]["lifetime"] == "per_call":
            assert group["adaptive"]["stats"]["target_transactions"] == group["fixed4"]["stats"]["target_transactions"]
    artifact = {"rows": all_rows, "traces": traces, "aggregate": {k: dict(v) for k, v in grouped.items()}}
    encoded = json.dumps(artifact, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
    path = Path("policy_lifecycle_results.json")
    path.write_text(encoded)
    print(json.dumps({"status": "PASS", "rows": len(all_rows), "paired_output_groups": len(pairs),
                      "artifact": str(path), "artifact_sha256": hashlib.sha256(encoded.encode()).hexdigest(),
                      "aggregate": artifact["aggregate"],
                      "limits": "Constructed 113-token streams and CPU oracle; no GPU score. Shared-question stress uses compatible equal trajectories; provenance still ambiguous."}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def stage(directory, arms):
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    source = (ROOT / "method.py").read_text()
    manifest = {"status": "STAGED_NOT_EVALUATED", "base_sha256": sha(ROOT / "method.py"), "arms": {}}
    for arm in arms:
        target = directory / arm / "method.py"
        target.parent.mkdir()
        target.write_text(source + ARMS[arm])
        compile(target.read_text(), str(target), "exec")
        manifest["arms"][arm] = {"path": str(target.resolve()), "sha256": sha(target), "entrypoint": "draft"}
    (directory / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
    return manifest


def run(directory, studies):
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    manifest = {"python": sys.version, "platform": platform.platform(),
                "started_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                "supporting_source_sha256": {p.name: sha(p) for p in sorted(ROOT.glob("*.py"))},
                "method_sha256": sha(ROOT / "method.py"), "runs": [],
                "scope": "CPU only; no target score. Legacy producers may update their documented artifacts."}
    for name in studies:
        args, required = STUDIES[name]
        missing = [p for p in required if not (ROOT / p).is_file()]
        if missing:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"{name}: unavailable archived inputs {missing}; run its producer only for a concrete new research need")
        command = [sys.executable] + args
        started = time.monotonic()
        with (directory / (name + ".stdout")).open("wb") as out, (directory / (name + ".stderr")).open("wb") as err:
            result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, stdout=out, stderr=err, check=False)
        row = {"study": name, "command": command, "returncode": result.returncode,
               "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started,
               "source_sha256": sha(ROOT / args[0]),
               "stdout_sha256": sha(directory / (name + ".stdout")),
               "stderr_sha256": sha(directory / (name + ".stderr"))}
        manifest["runs"].append(row)
        manifest["status"] = "PASS" if result.returncode == 0 else "FAIL"
        (directory / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
        if result.returncode:
            raise SystemExit(result.returncode)
    return manifest


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("catalog")
    p = sub.add_parser("run")
    p.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--studies", nargs="+", choices=STUDIES, default=["optimization", "lifecycle", "paired_analysis", "contract"])
    p = sub.add_parser("stage")
    p.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--arms", nargs="+", choices=ARMS, default=["abstention", "fixed2", "fixed4", "adaptive"])
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "catalog":
        print(json.dumps({k: {"argv": v[0], "missing_inputs": [p for p in v[1] if not (ROOT / p).exists()]} for k, v in STUDIES.items()}, indent=2))
    elif args.command == "stage":
        print(json.dumps(stage(args.output_dir, args.arms), indent=2))
    else:
        run(args.output_dir, args.studies)


if __name__ == "__main__":

This is pre-score research in the current track. The trusted GPU CLI is not yet

been measured. The mandatory cumulative 10 effective research hours remain
incomplete; the journal contains the conservative ledger and continuation point.

## Completed work

- Reviewed the instruction, current policy/notes, entire journal, prior plans,
  source and retained outputs. CPU evidence establishes contract behavior and
  simulator invariants; actual response repetition and verifier cost are unknown.
- Kept the corrected adaptive observed-ID policy. Removed duplicate validation
  of its already validated 96-ID search window and repeated allowance reads.
  `method_before_runner_optimization.py` preserves the incoming implementation.
  Differential verification matched 32,000 decisions and complete track states.

  response rows and 2,524 four-arm paired groups in `policy_lifecycle_results.json`.
  A lossless `.json.gz` copy preserves the same full evidence for resume bundles;
  the verifier accepts that copy if the uncompressed artifact is unavailable.
  Every paired CPU output agrees; separate accounting uses the saved artifact.

  logged subprocesses and self-contained staged policies. Actual commands, source
  hashes, stdout/stderr hashes, exits and runtime are retained in
  `research_preparation_results/manifest.json`. All four preparation studies pass.
- Added `paired_gpu_analysis.py`: complete five-seed pairing, frozen metadata and
  quality checks, question-cluster bootstrap and bounded promotion rules. Its
  self-test uses tagged synthetic CPU rows; no fabricated GPU export was written.

Useful within-response repetition may amortize block overhead (H1), or low
coverage/rejection/transport may make abstention fastest (H0). Acceptance alone
cannot choose a policy. Prior synthetic fixed4 sometimes beats adaptation;
early-cap observer fixes correct logic but do not establish latency superiority.

The new no-bonus/no-omission aggregate over stable, shifted and alternating
streams gives 2,144 adaptive target transactions at 16 shared tracks. At 17
shared tracks it gives 2,261, exactly the fixed4 count, with 1,294 pending
callbacks arriving without a retained track. Per-response persistent adaptation
at 17 tracks uses 2,278 transactions, while per-call recreation uses 2,261.
These counts compare constructed streams, not mean target latency. At 16 shared
tracks the no-horizon control uses 2,128 transactions; removing cooldown leaves
2,144 in this slice. Therefore horizon and cooldown should be tested separately
only when actual public evidence supports adaptation (H2).

for the cold path, 28.508/28.498 us stateless, and 17.338/17.565 us for mixed

implementation change removes proven duplicate work and preserves behavior.

- Public executor lifetime, actual concurrency, request identity, skipped calls,

- Target repeat frequency, accepted-prefix distribution and block/rollback cost.

### Independent speculative-index and rollback simulator (2026-10-05)

The trusted GPU scorer was still unavailable, so I added the independent CPU
simulator `speculative_index_rollback.py`. It defines a sequential oracle and a
separate indexed-cache implementation. A proposal is clipped to
`min(32, maximum_draft_tokens, remaining_tokens)`. The oracle compares from the
committed history index, accepts a matching prefix, emits one target token on
the first mismatch, and stops at an accepted or replacement EOS. The corrected
cache stages candidates at absolute indices, commits the accepted prefix, and
deletes every staged entry beginning at the first rejected index (or after an
accepted EOS). Explicit replay keys return the saved transaction without
mutating either state; this is a simulator invariant and is not an assumption
about a hidden host request ID.

The fixed matrix has 16 cases: zero acceptance, full acceptance, rejection at
all five positions of a four-token-plus-EOS target (including mismatch at EOS),
accepted EOS with trailing candidates, terminal replacement, EOS-candidate
replacement on an ordinary token, five maximum/remaining budget combinations,
and replay. All cases agree between oracle and corrected cache. A seeded
randomized differential run (`seed=20261005 ^ 0x5A17`) covered 10,000 operation
sequences with random target lengths, proposals of length 0..40, negative and
oversized budgets, remaining-token clipping, terminal tokens and replay calls;
the corrected implementation returned `PASS` with no differential failure.

    expected = {(case, seed, repeat, arm) for case in cases for seed in SEEDS for repeat in repeats for arm in arms}
    index = {}

        index[key] = row

    candidates = [arm for arm in arms if arm != "abstention"]

    for case in cases:

Stricter reuse lost useful repeats even for short-option questions, while option completion added rejected drafts when wording changed. It also produced eight lexical mismatches on exact echoes; I’ll test whether the 64-character payload limit caused those failures.

Whole-word payload truncation removed those eight mismatches in the lexical CPU test; changed echoes still caused rejected drafts, as expected. I’ll keep the incumbent unchanged and stage the competitors for GPU testing. I’ll also replace the old first-ten pilot, which covers only coarse perception, with 24 questions balanced across the six categories and reserve 72 for GPU validation.
